guarantees.claim: When EnMasking is true, zero_with_endbit[0] is driven to all zeros.
When EnMasking is true, zero_with_endbit[1][MsgWidth-1] is driven to end_of_block, and zero_with_endbit[1][MsgWidth-2:0] to zero.
When EnMasking is false, zero_with_endbit[0][MsgWidth-1] is driven to end_of_block, and zero_with_endbit[0][MsgWidth-2:0] to zero.
When EnMasking is false, zero_with_endbit[1] is not assigned by this block and remains undriven.
keccak_addr_o is assigned sent_message if sent_message < block_addr_limit, otherwise it is assigned '0.

assumptions.claim: end_of_block is correctly asserted at the appropriate cycle to indicate the end of the message block for zero padding.
assumptions.risk: Incorrect padding leading to hash mismatch or state corruption.

assumptions.claim: Downstream logic using keccak_addr_o must gate or safely handle writes when keccak_addr_o is driven to '0 due to sent_message >= block_addr_limit.
assumptions.risk: Inadvertent overwrite of data at address 0 if writes are not qualified.

uncertain_points.claim: When sent_message >= block_addr_limit, keccak_addr_o defaults to '0. It is unclear whether this wrap-around is intentional or a design gap that could overwrite the first block.
uncertain_points.risk: Data corruption or loss of previously written block at address 0.

uncertain_points.claim: When EnMasking is false, zero_with_endbit[1] is undriven. It is unknown whether any downstream consumer reads this share.
uncertain_points.risk: X propagation to outputs or state if the undriven share is used.
